free_tier.stated: A tilde community that is now a memorial: quoted 'The service was available for a total of five years coming to an end Feburary 2026' and 'This website now exists as a memorial for dimension and what it represented over the years'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: None; recorded to keep the tildeverse directory from being trusted as a liveness source.
limits_note: The host closed in February 2026 and the site now serves the closure notice, so nothing binds because nothing is offered.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the service closed, so no signup requirement could be read; the record's evidence covers the closure ('The service was available for a total of five years coming to an end Feburary 2026' and 'This website now exists as a memorial') and a stale tildeverse directory entry that still links a signup form.

evidence.proved: 'dimension.sh came online 26th June 2020, running CentOS 8 at Digital Ocean UK, and was open to new members on the 3rd July 2020. The service was available for a total of five years coming to an end Feburary 2026, mostly due to a combination of maintance overhead for the aging CentOS install, and a lack of usage. This website now exists as a memorial', quoted
the tildeverse directory still lists dimension.sh with a signup form and no closure marker, quoted, so the directory is stale and the first-party page is the authority

notes: Recorded as a refutation of the tildeverse directory rather than of any prior corpus claim. The directory page at tilde.team/wiki/other-tildes was read today and still carries a 'signup form' link for dimension.sh, protocol.club is marked 'closed' in the same table, and goober.cloud sits behind an Anubis proof-of-work wall. A reader who works from that table would chase at least one dead host. What would have made this a live row: an operator page with a signup form, which the first-party site no longer has.
